media:group.media:title: JAL 123 Stayed Airborne for 30 Minutes Without its Tail Fin 😨 Air Disasters | Smithsonian Channel
media:group.media:description:
Investigators looking into the deadly August 13, 1985 crash of JAL 123 discover that the cabin’s pressurized air may have caused the plane’s faulty tail fin to rip off, mid flight. Amazingly, the crew were able to keep the 747 flying for around 30 minutes before it crashed.

entry.title: How Alaskan Rescue Choppers Can Keep Flying for Over 14 Hours | Ice Airport Alaska | Smithsonian

media:group.media:title: How Alaskan Rescue Choppers Can Keep Flying for Over 14 Hours | Ice Airport Alaska | Smithsonian
media:group.media:description:
100 miles north of Anchorage, a Pave Hawk rescue chopper approaches a hovering HC-130, and performs a mid-air refuelling. Alaska is a huge state, and rescues can take over 14 hours—far beyond the capacity of a Pave Hawk which only has a range of about 400 miles.

entry.title: Loading a 10,000 Pound Engine into a 737 Without a Crane | Ice Airport Alaska | Smithsonian

media:group.media:title: Loading a 10,000 Pound Engine into a 737 Without a Crane | Ice Airport Alaska | Smithsonian
media:group.media:description:
The Alaska Airlines maintenance team are working to install a $10 million replacement engine into a sidelined 737. To pick the engine up, they install a system of geared chains called ‘bootstraps’—essentially using the weight of the plane and engine for leverage.

media:group.media:title: Two Engineers Hustle to Repair a Cell Tower Before Night | Ice Airport Alaska | Smithsonian
media:group.media:description:
Two engineers are racing to fix a broken cell tower that connects a small Alaskan town to the outside world. An Alpha Aviation pilot is scheduled to pick them up once their job is done—but he needs to do that before darkness descends and the terrain below is no longer visible.
